wakesOne: {disks} is asleep and spins up now, this takes a few seconds
wakesMany: {disks} are asleep and spin up now, this takes a few seconds
parityTip: Runs on the server, big jobs wait until it is done
parityPausedTip: Paused right now, your jobs run as usual meanwhile
parityDone: The parity check is done, waiting jobs carry on now
diskShareTip: You are right on {disk}. Do not copy or move between here and /mnt/user, or Unraid may cut files to 0 bytes.
diskAsleep: The disk is asleep, the list comes from the index.
toPrimary: New files land on {pool}, the mover fetches what is left on the array ({disks}).
toSecondary: New files land on {pool}, the mover takes them to {disks} {when}.

waiting.one: One file with {size} is still on {pool} here.
waiting.other: {n} files with {size} are still on {pool} here.

cacheFile: Still on {pool}, the mover takes the file to the array
cacheDir: Something in here is still on {pool}
moonTip: {disk} is asleep. CannonCommander shows its folders from the index, only opening a file wakes it.

perms.title: Set permissions the Unraid way
perms.ownerTip: This is how files on Unraid belong to the shares, the Docker containers and the network alike.
perms.rightsTip: Everyone may read and write, folders can be opened. No file is executable afterwards.
perms.warnText: Everything in {name} gets these permissions, also files you set up differently on purpose.
perms.keptSome: These folders stay as they are:
perms.keptNone: Nothing in here needs to be left out.
perms.blockedArchive: Nothing can be changed inside an archive.
perms.blockedText: {path} belongs to {own}. Containers, VMs or the stick need their own owners and permissions there.
perms.background: Runs as a job in the background
perms.failed: Setting permissions in {name} did not work: {error}

where.title: Location
where.onTip: The disk or pool the data really lies on. The user share below /mnt/user shows all disks together.
where.linksTip: The same file also lies under these paths. It takes its space only once. Copying or moving across a share turns them into files of their own.
